claim: Stress is a potent modulator of the mammalian brain.

claim: The stress hormone response influences many brain regions, particularly the hippocampus.

claim: Acute stress increased hippocampal cell proliferation.

claim: 2 weeks, but not 2 days, after acute stress, rats showed enhanced fear extinction memory.

claim: Brief stress has a beneficial role for the hippocampus.

claim: Chronic stress leads to cardiovascular disease, obesity, depression, and exacerbation of neurodegeneration.

claim: An inverted U function explains the variable consequences of acute stress for brain health.

claim: Brief or moderate stressors enhance neural function while severe or prolonged stressors are detrimental.

claim: Moderate stress enhances memory performance in rodents.

claim: The hippocampus is exquisitely sensitive to stress and glucocorticoids.

claim: The dentate gyrus has a high density of glucocorticoid receptors.
source_text: Within the dentate gyrus (DG) sub-region, in particular, there exists a high density of GC receptors that respond to elevated circulating GCs (De Kloet et al., 1998).

claim: The dentate gyrus is strongly connected to the basolateral amygdala via the entorhinal cortex and medial septum.
source_text: In addition, the DG is strongly connected via the entorhinal cortex and medial septum to the basolateral amygdala (BLA), a brain region involved in emotional processing and an important mediator of many stress effects on the hippocampus (McGaugh, 2004).

claim: Early work indicated suppression of proliferation following acute stress or glucocorticoid injection.
source_text: While early work indicated suppression of proliferation following acute stress or GC injection (Cameron and Gould, 1994; Gould et al., 1997), subsequent studies have yielded mixed results, often reporting no change in proliferation following a variety of acute stressors (Thomas et al., 2006; Thomas et al., 2007; Dagyte et al., 2009; Hanson et al., 2011).

claim: Acute stress enhances expression of mitogenic growth factors such as FGF2 and NGF.

claim: Acute exercise increases neurogenesis in the adult hippocampus.

claim: Acute stress may be beneficial for brain health in general and hippocampal plasticity in particular.
source_text: These studies, along with our findings, evoke the interesting possibility that acute stress may be beneficial for brain health in general and hippocampal plasticity in particular.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference (indicated by 'may' and 'possibility') drawn from multiple studies including the current findings.

claim: Acute CORT enhanced proliferation in well-handled, habituated rats.
source_text: Notably, while we found that acute CORT enhanced proliferation in well-handled, habituated rats, we did not find any effect of acute CORT on neurogenesis in rats that were not habituated to injection.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data comparing habituated and non-habituated rats.

claim: Acute CORT had no effect on neurogenesis in rats that were not habituated to injection.
source_text: Notably, while we found that acute CORT enhanced proliferation in well-handled, habituated rats, we did not find any effect of acute CORT on neurogenesis in rats that were not habituated to injection.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from non-habituated rats.

claim: Factors present before the stressor begins may alter the effect of acute stress.
source_text: Our findings therefore demonstrate that factors present before the stressor begins may alter the effect of acute stress, perhaps by changing the susceptibility of controls or stressed animals to manipulation.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the differential effects observed in habituated vs non-habituated rats.

claim: The single prolonged stress model of PTSD uses three acute stressors in series (restraint, forced swim and ether) and results in delayed deficits in fear extinction and enhanced anxiety.
source_text: Most prominently, the single prolonged stress model of PTSD uses three acute stressors in series (restraint, forced swim and ether) and results in delayed deficits in fear extinction, as well as enhanced anxiety (Knox et al., 2012a, 2012b).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Knox et al., 2012a, 2012b.

claim: If any one of the three components of the single prolonged stress protocol are eliminated, deficits are no longer evident.
source_text: However, if any one of the three components of this stressor protocol are eliminated, deficits are no longer evident (Knox et al., 2012a), suggesting that stressor effects depend on the severity and length of the stressor, perhaps following the inverted U function previously described (Lupien and McEwen, 1997).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Knox et al., 2012a.

claim: Stressor effects depend on the severity and length of the stressor.
source_text: However, if any one of the three components of this stressor protocol are eliminated, deficits are no longer evident (Knox et al., 2012a), suggesting that stressor effects depend on the severity and length of the stressor, perhaps following the inverted U function previously described (Lupien and McEwen, 1997).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the cited work and related to the inverted U model.

claim: Mild early life stress can lead to resilience against stress later in life in multiple non-human primate species.
source_text: In multiple non-human primate species, for example, mild early life stress can lead to resilience against stress later in life, a phenomenon referred to as stress inoculation (Lyons and Parker, 2007; Katz et al., 2009; Parker and Maestripiero, 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Lyons and Parker, 2007; Katz et al., 2009; Parker and Maestripiero, 2011.

claim: More severe early life stress can increase stress vulnerability later in adulthood.
source_text: In contrast, more severe early life stress can have the opposite outcome, increasing stress vulnerability later in adulthood.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established knowledge about early life stress effects, contrasting with stress inoculation.

claim: At high, traumatic levels, acute stress may result in maladaptive pathology.
source_text: At high, traumatic levels, acute stress may result in maladaptive pathology (e.g., PTSD-like symptoms in the single prolonged stress model).
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference (indicated by 'may') based on the inverted U model and PTSD literature.

claim: At moderate levels, acute stress may actually enhance function.
source_text: At more moderate levels, though, such as immobilization in well-handled rats, acute stress may actually enhance function.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference (indicated by 'may') based on the current study's findings.

claim: Many acute-stress-induced changes in hippocampal plasticity rely on functional input from the BLA.
source_text: Many acute-stress-induced changes in hippocampal plasticity rely on functional input from the BLA.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established knowledge about BLA involvement in stress effects.

claim: Stress enhances hippocampal memory consolidation and LTP, but lesion of the BLA blocks these enhancements.
source_text: For example, while stress enhances hippocampal memory consolidation and LTP, lesion of the BLA blocks these enhancements (Quirarte et al., 1997; Roozendaal et al., 2009a, 2009b).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Quirarte et al., 1997; Roozendaal et al., 2009a, 2009b.

claim: Hippocampal cell proliferation and the activation of newborn neurons in a fear-conditioning paradigm both depend on BLA neural input.
source_text: We have recently reported that hippocampal cell proliferation and the activation of the newborn neurons in a fear-conditioning paradigm both depend on BLA neural input (Kirby et al., 2012b).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work, Kirby et al., 2012b.

claim: Acute stress regulation of neurogenesis may not rely on the same systems-level in vivo circuitry that mediates acute stress regulation of memory consolidation and LTP.
source_text: These findings imply that acute stress regulation of neurogenesis may not rely on the same systems-level in vivo circuitry that mediates acute stress regulation of memory consolidation and LTP.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the finding that BLA lesion did not affect stress-induced neurogenesis.

claim: NPCs did not respond to acute CORT treatment independently in vitro.
source_text: We found that while NPCs did not respond to acute CORT treatment independently in vitro, they did proliferate more in response to conditioned media from CORT-treated primary astrocytes, suggesting a role for secreted factors from local astrocytes in mediating stress effects on NPCs.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in vitro experimental data showing no direct CORT effect on NPCs.

claim: NPCs proliferate more in response to conditioned media from CORT-treated primary astrocytes.
source_text: We found that while NPCs did not respond to acute CORT treatment independently in vitro, they did proliferate more in response to conditioned media from CORT-treated primary astrocytes, suggesting a role for secreted factors from local astrocytes in mediating stress effects on NPCs.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in vitro experimental data using astrocyte conditioned media.

claim: Secreted factors from local astrocytes mediate stress effects on NPCs.
source_text: We found that while NPCs did not respond to acute CORT treatment independently in vitro, they did proliferate more in response to conditioned media from CORT-treated primary astrocytes, suggesting a role for secreted factors from local astrocytes in mediating stress effects on NPCs.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the conditioned media experiments.

claim: Astrocytes play a dynamic role in facilitating neuronal function through secreted factors.
source_text: The dynamic role of astrocytes in facilitating neuronal function through secreted factors has gained much recognition (Eroglu and Barres, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Eroglu and Barres, 2010.

claim: Astrocytes aid in synaptic glutamate recycling.
source_text: In addition to aiding in synaptic glutamate recycling, astrocytes secrete several factors such as thrombospondins (Eroglu and Barres, 2010), Hevin, SPARC (Kucukdereli et al., 2011) and glypicans (Allen et al., 2012) that regulate synaptic formation and function in mature neurons (Eroglu and Barres, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Eroglu and Barres, 2010.

claim: Astrocytes secrete thrombospondins, Hevin, SPARC and glypicans that regulate synaptic formation and function in mature neurons.
source_text: In addition to aiding in synaptic glutamate recycling, astrocytes secrete several factors such as thrombospondins (Eroglu and Barres, 2010), Hevin, SPARC (Kucukdereli et al., 2011) and glypicans (Allen et al., 2012) that regulate synaptic formation and function in mature neurons (Eroglu and Barres, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Eroglu and Barres, 2010; Kucukdereli et al., 2011; Allen et al., 2012.

claim: Astrocytes express the glucocorticoid receptor, GR.
source_text: Astrocytes express the glucocorticoid receptor, GR, and when they are exposed to high levels of GCs, GC-bound GR translocates to the nucleus and enhances FGF2 gene transcription (Molteni et al., 2001; Gubba et al., 2004; Unemura et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Molteni et al., 2001; Gubba et al., 2004; Unemura et al., 2012.

claim: When astrocytes are exposed to high levels of glucocorticoids, GC-bound GR translocates to the nucleus and enhances FGF2 gene transcription.
source_text: Astrocytes express the glucocorticoid receptor, GR, and when they are exposed to high levels of GCs, GC-bound GR translocates to the nucleus and enhances FGF2 gene transcription (Molteni et al., 2001; Gubba et al., 2004; Unemura et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Molteni et al., 2001; Gubba et al., 2004; Unemura et al., 2012.

claim: FGF2 is a potent and necessary proliferative factor in adult NPCs.
source_text: FGF2 is a potent and necessary proliferative factor in adult NPCs (Chipperfield et al., 2002).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Chipperfield et al., 2002.

claim: Acute stress stimulated FGF2 expression in the dorsal hippocampus and in primary hippocampal astrocytes.
source_text: We found that acute stress stimulated FGF2 expression in the dorsal hippocampus and in primary hippocampal astrocytes.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemical data.

claim: In the dentate gyrus and hilus, the enhancement in FGF2 levels following stress is largely restricted to GFAP+ astrocytes.
source_text: We further showed that in the DG and hilus, the enhancement in FGF2 levels following stress is largely restricted to GFAP+ astrocytes.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by confocal microscopy data showing FGF2 colocalization with GFAP.

claim: Changes in FGF2 protein levels following acute stress closely paralleled the neurogenic response.
source_text: Notably, changes in FGF2 protein levels following acute stress closely paralleled the neurogenic response; that is, FGF2 levels were increased only in stress conditions that also stimulated neurogenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is a correlative observation from comparing FGF2 and proliferation data across conditions.

claim: Neutralizing the astrocyte-secreted FGF2 prevented enhanced proliferation in cultured NPCs.
source_text: Neutralizing the astrocyte-secreted FGF2 prevented enhanced proliferation in cultured NPCs.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in vitro experiments using FGF2 neutralizing antibody.

claim: Astrocytes support hippocampal plasticity in response to an environmental stressor through secreted FGF2.
source_text: These findings suggest a novel role for astrocytes in supporting hippocampal plasticity in response to an environmental stressor through secreted FGF2.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the combined in vivo and in vitro findings about FGF2's role.

claim: Newly-born neurons are implicated in numerous hippocampal memory functions.
source_text: Newly-born neurons are implicated in numerous hippocampal memory functions (Aimone et al., 2010), particularly contextual fear conditioning.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Aimone et al., 2010.

claim: Contextual fear conditioning activates immature neurons.
source_text: Contextual fear conditioning activates immature neurons (Kirby et al., 2012b) and when new neurons are selectively knocked down, fear extinction is impaired (Deng et al., 2009; Stone et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Kirby et al., 2012b.

claim: When new neurons are selectively knocked down, fear extinction is impaired.
source_text: Contextual fear conditioning activates immature neurons (Kirby et al., 2012b) and when new neurons are selectively knocked down, fear extinction is impaired (Deng et al., 2009; Stone et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Deng et al., 2009 and Stone et al., 2010.

claim: Prolonging survival of newly-born neurons through targeted knockdown of apoptotic pathways enhances discrimination between similar contexts in a fear conditioning task.
source_text: Sahay et al. have further shown that prolonging survival of newly-born neurons through targeted knockdown of apoptotic pathways enhances discrimination between similar contexts in a fear conditioning task (Sahay et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Sahay et al., 2011.

claim: The 2-week time window coincides with the period in which newborn cells are hyper-plastic and more likely to be recruited to active circuitry.
source_text: This time window coincides with the period in which the newborn cells are hyper-plastic and more likely to be recruited to active circuitry (Kee et al., 2007; Deng et al., 2009; Kirby et al., 2012b).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Kee et al., 2007; Deng et al., 2009; Kirby et al., 2012b.

claim: Immobilized rats better utilize the pool of immature neurons, possibly contributing to their enhanced memory.
source_text: Given that immobilized rats had a similar number of newborn neurons as controls, these data suggest that immobilized rats better utilize the pool of immature neurons, possibly contributing to their enhanced memory.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference (indicated by 'suggest' and 'possibly') drawn from the activation and behavioral data.

claim: The dorsal hippocampus supports spatial and declarative memory while the ventral hippocampus facilitates affective regulation.
source_text: A recent hypothesis posits that the dorsal and ventral hippocampus support different behavioral functions, with the dorsal region being important for spatial and declarative memory while the ventral region facilitates affective regulation (Fanselow and Dong, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Fanselow and Dong, 2010.

claim: Chronic stress preferentially affects the ventral over the dorsal hippocampus.
source_text: This division may also apply to neural stem cell regulation within the DG of each region where chronic stress preferentially effects the ventral over the dorsal hippocampus, perhaps reflecting the negative affective consequences of chronic stress (Tanti et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Tanti et al., 2012.

claim: The memory benefits observed 2 weeks after stress were in contextual fear extinction, a task that relies on spatial memory hypothesized to depend on the dorsal dentate gyrus.
source_text: Moreover, the memory benefits observed 2 weeks after stress were in contextual fear extinction, a task that relies on the kind of spatial memory hypothesized to depend on the dorsal DG (Fanselow and Dong, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This combines the behavioral findings with the cited hypothesis about dorsal hippocampal function.

claim: The selective involvement of the dorsal hippocampus implies that the acute stressor model functions as a cognitive stimulant for the declarative domains of hippocampal function rather than as a modulator of emotional responsivity.
source_text: This selective involvement of the dorsal hippocampus implies that our acute stressor model functions as a cognitive stimulant for the declarative domains of hippocampal function rather than as a modulator of emotional responsivity.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the regional specificity of the stress effects.

claim: Moderate, acute stress may stimulate heightened brain plasticity via increased neurogenesis.
source_text: The current study suggests that moderate, acute stress may stimulate heightened brain plasticity via increased neurogenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is an overall inference drawn from the study's findings, indicated by 'suggests' and 'may'.
